clue.text: Nearest neighbours exemplify tact, initially holding vote

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the three preceding words
holding means the letters taken keep something else inside them

blocks.note: the first letters of these three words
a cross on a ballot paper is a vote

explanation.surface: People living close by show tactfulness by first holding a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearest neighbours' reads as one phrase, but only 'Nearest' is the definition; the initials start with 'neighbours'.
explanation.definitionFit: The next house is the closest one, so next is a synonym for nearest.

clue.text: Isolated group subject turns son into Conservative

indicators.note: turns one thing into another means one letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: to subject a people is to enslave them
S is the abbreviation for son
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A cut-off community whose topic swings a boy into voting Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a noun (a topic), but it is the verb meaning to dominate.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a distinct community or territory surrounded by a different one, so a group set apart.

clue.text: Run into train track

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: the train of a dress or comet is its tail
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone sprints onto a railway line in front of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway picture makes 'train' a locomotive; here it is the trailing part of a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or the marks left behind, the same as a track.

clue.text: Police deployed around pound arresting rogue for minor sin

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread out and rearranged, so the letters are reorganised
around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
arresting means seizing and holding something inside

blocks.note: taken as written
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Officers sent out around town, pulling in a scoundrel, all for a trivial offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers stack here: the jumbled letters first take in the pound sign, and that result then takes in the rogue near its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small fault or trivial offence, from the Spanish for little sin.

clue.text: Withdrawn hint is mine

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a tip is a hint

explanation.surface: A shy person claims a clue as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive pronoun; it is the noun, a place where coal is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a coal mine, the usual British word for a colliery.

clue.text: Stirs just over half of food round?

indicators.note: taking just over half of a word means a little less than its back half is cut away

blocks.note: a comestible is an item of food
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: Someone mixes a bit more than half a portion of food in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the ten letters of COMESTIBLE is just over half. 'Stirs' looks like mixing, but here it means waking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs after fainting or sleeping regains consciousness, which is what comes to means.

clue.text: Suppositions Maoists spun freely

indicators.note: spun freely suggests letters whirled loose and landing in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Guesses that Chinese communists put about without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' does double duty in the surface, but its letters are part of the fodder and 'spun freely' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposition is something taken for granted without proof, the same as an assumption.

clue.text: Disorderly old tax collectors going as predicted?

blocks.note: IR is Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
something regular keeps to a predictable pattern

explanation.surface: Former taxmen behaving unpredictably while things go to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was merged into HMRC in 2005, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular means not following order or rule, so disorderly is a close synonym.

clue.text: Doris, say, arguably more "out" before end of evening

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: being less in can be argued to be being more out
the last letter of evening

explanation.surface: A woman named Doris, perhaps more openly gay, before the evening ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Lessing was the British Nobel-winning novelist; 'say' marks her as an example of someone with that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing, author of The Golden Notebook, is the famous bearer of this surname, so she is an instance.

clue.text: One month besieging Brown Sector

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: October, abbreviated, is a single month
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: For a month a man called Brown lays siege to a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' sits capitalised like a surname but is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is an eighth part of a circle, a sector bounded by two radii at 45 degrees.

clue.text: Bit on the side in Paris very inspired by escape

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to escape something is to miss it
very in French

explanation.surface: An affair in Paris that is very much prompted by a desire for escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to use French.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is informal for a secret lover of a married person, which a mistress is.

clue.text: Docked in unusually still sea

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an unexpected order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship moored in waters that are oddly calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The sea picture makes 'Docked' a ship in port; it means having had a tail cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog or horse whose tail has been docked has had it cut off, leaving it without one.

clue.text: Unbounded sport expertise starts to enrich new county town

indicators.note: without bounds means the outermost letters at each end are dropped
starts to points to the opening letters of the next words

blocks.note: tennis is a sport
skill is expertise
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Unlimited sporting talent first helps to boost a fresh town's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: Enniskillen is the county town of Fermanagh in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county town is the administrative centre of a county, as Enniskillen is for Fermanagh.

clue.text: Hoarder's minute silver dish

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for minute
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: A collector's tiny silver plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like the adjective tiny, but it is the unit of time. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is famed for collecting shiny objects, so a person who hoards trinkets is called one.

clue.text: Sharing cost of portion alfresco?

blocks.note: a helping is a portion of food
alfresco means in the open air, outdoors

explanation.surface: Splitting the bill for a meal eaten outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the charade reading is playful: a helping eaten out.
explanation.definitionFit: To help out with a bill is to contribute to it, so someone sharing the cost is helping out.

clue.text: Old place name red-top rag reprinted

indicators.note: reprinted means set again, so the letters are reset in a different order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper rerun with an outdated city name.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid, so called from its red masthead; a rag is a poor newspaper. Petrograd was St Petersburg's name from 1914 to 1924.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrograd is the former name of St Petersburg, later Leningrad, so it is an old place name.

clue.text: Sport gun Republican avoids

indicators.note: avoids means keeps away from, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: a Luger is a German pistol
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A sport in which a political figure steers clear of firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: The luge is a winter Olympic event racing a small sled feet first, so a sport.

clue.text: Contraction of insanity intermittently observed

indicators.note: something seen only intermittently shows up every other moment, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Signs of madness are noticed only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contraction' sounds medical but means a shortened word with an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Isn't is the shortened form of is not, the kind of word grammar calls a contraction.

clue.text: Law takes time to block representation

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so one letter sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: a statue is a representation of a figure
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Legislation takes a while to get in the way of fair representation.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Toy hippos loosely stuffed with twisted rag -- that's about right

indicators.note: loosely means not held in order, so the letters are rearranged
twisted means turned out of shape, so these letters too are jumbled
stuffed with means filled, so one set of letters goes inside another
about means placed around, so everything else surrounds one letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A stuffed hippo toy, loosely filled with an old cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the hippos and the rag are jumbled; the 'about' then wraps the whole lot round the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirograph is a classic drawing toy of toothed plastic gears and rings that trace looping patterns.

clue.text: Mike, flexible, fully promotes one prosthetic filler

indicators.note: promoting something all the way sends it right to the top, so that letter moves to the front

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
pliant means flexible

explanation.surface: A supple man called Mike wholeheartedly backs a single artificial part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the Roman numeral I already in PLIANT; in a down clue promotion means moving up, so that I climbs to the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: An implant is an artificial device placed in the body, such as a dental or breast implant, filling a space.

clue.text: Sharp play on words chap supports

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this word comes after the other

blocks.note: a pun is a play on words
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A man backs a cutting witticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means sharply strong in smell or taste, or biting in remark.

clue.text: Layman apolitically embraces a vision to die for?

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the letters sit inside the words before it

blocks.note: inside layMAN APOLItically

explanation.surface: An unaffiliated layperson takes in a heavenly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'See Naples and die'; Napoli is the Italian name for Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one should see Naples and then die, since nothing afterwards could match the view.

clue.text: Put off after page 1

blocks.note: post means after, as in post-war
P is the abbreviation for page
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: An instruction to defer until after the first page.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to delay something to a later time, which is what put off means.

clue.text: Exercise strategy that goes up to 11?

blocks.note: a plan is a strategy
the alphabet's eleventh letter, where counting A to K goes up to 11

explanation.surface: A workout plan whose intensity is turned up to eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes up to 11' echoes the amplifier joke from the film This Is Spinal Tap.
explanation.definitionFit: The plank is a core exercise in which the body is held straight and rigid, like a board.

clue.text: 7 band member tipped 3 to cavort with 16

indicators.note: tipped means having its tip taken off, so the first letter goes
cavorting means leaping about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: the answer to 3 down
the answer to 16 across

explanation.surface: A band member, with track and sled entries, jumping about.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to IRREGULAR, so the definition is a member of an irregular band of fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerilla fights in an irregular, unofficial force rather than a regular army.

clue.text: Braggart turns out second hat

indicators.note: turns out means expels, so that letter is thrown out

blocks.note: a braggart is a boaster
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A show-off proves to be the runner-up hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' reads as 'proves to be', but means ejects.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat, traditionally worn for punting and rowing.

clue.text: Brother or sister pops up twice

indicators.note: in a down entry popping up means rising, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: sib is short for sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: A sibling appears for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bis is Latin for twice, used in music and addresses for repeat or encore.

clue.text: Distention following injury causes tissue inflammation

indicators.note: after injury something is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Swelling after an injury leads to soreness in the body's tissues.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a medical note, so 'following injury' passes as plain sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendonitis is the inflammation of a tendon, the fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Equipment located by English and Scottish corporation

blocks.note: kit is equipment
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Gear found by an English firm and a Scottish company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company, but it is the old jocular word for a pot belly; kite is Scots for belly.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect a kite is the belly or stomach, and corporation is an old humorous term for a paunch.
